text:
maria: Ran a quick sweep of the new attention-path sampler + kernel picker on the GQA/MQA combo. Found a regression when we use KV-page block_size=64 on A100 nodes — p95 token latency up and throughput down.

alex: Can you drop the numbers?

maria: Yup. Single-node A100, model=redwood/gqa-mqa-v1, seq=1024, batch=8: 
```bash
# baseline (picker v1, block=128)
p50=16.8ms p95=35.1ms throughput=134 tok/s
# experiment (picker v2, block=64)
p50=18.2ms p95=39.4ms throughput=110 tok/s
# worst case observed in canary run
p95=44.8ms, occasional 52-60ms spikes during KV page flips
```

sanjay: Those spikes smell like KV cache page boundary copies / extra memcpys. With MQA the KV layout is interleaved and block size 64 can cause more cross-page accesses.

lisa: Did you collect perf counters? L2 miss, dram bw?

maria: Quick perf stat dump from the run (NVIDIA Nsight sampling): 
```
L2_miss_rate: 0.12 -> 0.21 (baseline -> experiment)
DRAM_bw_util: 42% -> 67%
SM_eff: 82% -> 78%
Context_switches: spikes correlate with page boundary events
```

alex: Interesting. So block=64 increases L2 miss and DRAM pressure on A100. What about block=128?

maria: Re-ran with block=128 and same picker v2: p95 back to ~35-40ms, throughput +9%.

perf-bot: benchmark 2187654321-01: model=redwood/gqa-mqa-v1, seq=1024, batch=8, kernel=picker_v2, kv_block=64, p50=18.2ms, p95=39.4ms, tput=110 tok/s

sanjay: Hypothesis: our kernel selector currently biases by model/arch only, not by kv_block alignment. Need seqlen-aware + kv-layout-aware scoring. Also MQA introduces extra Q-stripes that change memory stride.

lisa: Proposal: add a microbench at node startup that probes small matrix-times for candidate block sizes (64/96/128) and a small KV-page prefetch trial. Store a per-GPU heuristic + a runtime override. That should avoid blanket picks that are bad on A100.

alex: Agree. Also tweak the batching heuristics to prefer batcher.max_batch_tokens=4096 for seqlen>=512 to reduce number of page flips per request.

maria: I'll prototype: kernel_picker:score += arch_bias + seqlen_bucket_bonus + kv_block_penalty. kv_block_penalty computed from microbench for this GPU arch. Plan to default to block=128 for A100 when avg seqlen>512.

sanjay: One caveat: on H100 80GB we saw the opposite earlier — block=64 had slightly lower L2 misses. So make sure microbench captures both cache and DRAM curves per architecture.

lisa: Also consider grouping KV pages in-memory when ephemeral batching is enabled so contiguous prefixes stay on same page -> reduces page churn. Might be a small allocator change.

maria: Command used for microbench prototype: 
```bash
./kv_microbench --gpu-query --model-shape gqa-mqa-v1 --try-blocks 64,96,128 --seqs 128,512,1024 --iters 50
```

alex: Can you open a PR with the picker change + microbench harness and perf artifacts? Gate behind runtime.autotune.kvblock=true. We'll run a canary on eng-runtime canary pool.

maria: Will do. Early diff will only add scoring hooks and the microbench, no default flips.

perf-bot: ci/workflows/bench: attached artifacts -> s3://redwood-perf/2187654321/ (contains nsight traces, microbench csvs) :eyes:

maria: CC @eng-runtime. Plan: land PR today, canary tonight, look for p95 regressions on seq=256/512/1024 across A100/H100. If regressions appear, rollback flag.

alex: Thanks — please include a short playbook in PR for how to interpret microbench csv (what metric to prefer: p95 token latency or DRAM bw).

maria: Will add docs and a small script to convert microbench CSV -> heuristic scores.

sanjay: Also log KV page flip events in runtime trace so we can correlate spike timestamps with requests.

lisa: I'll add a lightweight trace point. Minimal perf impact.

maria: OK, PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7423 — includes tests and artifacts. Planning canary at 23:00 UTC.

alex: Nice work. If canary looks good let's roll to dedicated test pool and then to prod. :thumbsup:
